    Wallet

    Your wallet is a 12-word recovery phrase. It lives on this PC with no password; the phrase is the only backup.

    Or restore

    Write these 12 words down. They are shown once, and they are the only way to recover your tags.
    —

    Import a wallet

    Paste a private key (WIF) or another wallet's 12 or 24 words; words give that wallet's first address. Kept here, encrypted; nothing is published.

    Accounts, sign-in and linked wallets

    Accounts

    AccountAddressFrom
    Sign in with a Dogecoin Arcade account

    Your account's words are kept on the arcade that holds your account, sealed under your password; any arcade hands out the sealed copy and only your password opens it, here on this PC. Your imported wallets, groups, address book and blocked list come with it. The password is not stored.

    @

    Linked wallets

    Attach another wallet on this chain to your @tag. The wallet's key and your @tag's key both sign the link, so other arcades can check it. The key is kept here, encrypted.

    @

      Messages are sealed on the Pepecoin testnet chain to the other person's key, and a copy to yours, so they come back when you restore your 12 words. Each one is a transaction with a small fee; old Dogecoin Arcade accounts can read and reply.

      API

      For programs on this computer (sidecar apps)

      JSON-RPC 2.0 at , every command, using the cookie file as Basic auth. Bitcoin-style clients work as is.

      For websites

      The web API at . Public reads need nothing; the rest need a key from below. It answers only this computer: a website you put online reaches it from its own server code, never visitors' browsers.

      Every command: GET /api/v1/routes or the method rpc.help. Full list in docs/API.md.

      Chains & Coins

      Coins

      Install a chain to keep it on this arcade; nothing is installed unless you do it here. Coins you haven't installed can be borrowed through other arcades' Core nodes: this arcade keeps only their block headers and your own coins, and checks every block it reads. Installing a chain replaces its borrowed copy.

      Get it from

      Arcades on the mesh first: other V1.0 arcades' blocks, or an existing arcade's Core node. This waits up to a minute and a half for their answers, then uses the coin's own P2P network for anything left.

        Mine testnet

        Mines Pepecoin testnet blocks on this PC and pays your wallet. Mined coins can be spent after 240 blocks (about 4 hours).

        Stakes this wallet's Kotia on this PC: every 16 seconds each coin with 20 confirmations gets a chance to make the next block, in proportion to its size. A staked block pays 20 KOT back to the same address, with the coin. Coins never leave your address. A block the network refuses changes nothing.

          —

          Off unless you turn it on. When on, this arcade looks for a new release every 6 hours and installs it by itself: the download is checked against the release's SHA-256, the old programs are kept beside the new ones (as .prev), and the service restarts cleanly. Your wallet, @handle, messages and chains stay as they are. If the app window is open, open it again after an update to load the new version.
